1343.evidence: Ambrosiana Q 123 sup. ff. 210-233 is a 16th-century set of copies of the papal Secretariat's 1563 cipher correspondence from Borromeo's papers. The letters run between Borromeo and the legate Morone, and from the nuncio in Spain Crivelli to Borromeo. The set is not the legates' own ciphers from Trent. Constant, La legation du cardinal Morone (1922; full text on archive.org, constantlecardinalmoro), identifies the leaves in two places. (1) p. 171 n. 6: Borromeo to Morone, the cipher of 8 June 1563. Its 'original chiffre, avec dechiffrement officiel' is in Vatican Concilio 29 n. 114, and its text is printed by Steinherz, Nuntiaturberichte II/3, p. 333. Constant adds: 'L'Ambroisienne en conserve une copie du 16e siecle (Q. 123, f. 222)'. (2) p. 172 n. 12: an Italian passage of Borromeo to Morone, 8 June 1563, is cited from Concilio 29 f. 116 and from 'Ambroisienne, Q.123, f. 227', with Sickel, Romische Berichte II, p. 62 n. 1. Both leaves lie in unit 21, 'Lettere cifrate' (ff. 221r-233r). The neighbouring unit 19 (ff. 215-217), Crivelli's 'Cifra' of 15 July 1563 on the Luna precedence, is printed in full by Constant as no. XXIII (pp. 435-440) from the Vatican copy of the official decipherment, Varia Politicorum 11 and 'Ambroisienne Q. 123 f. 215-217'. The heading 'Cifra di Mons. Crivello nuntio in Spagna' stands over a plain Italian text, so in this volume a 'cifra' heading marks a clear copy of a deciphered letter. The Luna precedence matter (unit 20) is the subject of Borromeo's cipher to Morone of 9 May 1563 'circa il dar luogo al conte di Luna', which Constant quotes on p. 142 n. 6 (cf. Sickel RB II 134), and of Pius IV's autograph of 8 May (Sickel RB II). The whole correspondence is edited: Steinherz NBD II/3, Sickel RB, Constant, and Susta vol. 4 for the legates' 1563 letters. Caveat: units 18 ('Lettera cifrata, 13 maggio 1563', ff. 210-212) and 20 (f. 219) are not individually matched to a printed letter, because the Ambrosiana OPAC sits behind a JS bot check and no browser was used. They belong to the same series of Secretariat copies, and nothing suggests surviving ciphertext without a decipherment. Lead 2200 (APUG, 'Cifra sopra il luogo del conte di Luna', 13 ff.) is another copy volume of the same 1563 correspondence and is covered by the same evidence. The catalogue's correspondents and place are also wrong: Borromeo (Rome) to the legate Morone, and Crivelli (Madrid) to Borromeo, not 'legates/nuncios at Trent'.

1345.evidence: Same letter as lead 2204, which was closed as read. The Ambrosiana OPAC title (X 279 inf.), 'Lettera in cifra di monsignor segretario di stato a sua santita mandata al cardinale Bichi nunzio in Francia intercettata dal governatore di Lione', repeats the heading that circulated with the plain text of this intercepted letter ('a sua santita' is very probably a misreading of 'di Sua Santita'). Four other manuscript copies with that heading are now on record. (1) Florence, Moreniana, Bigazzi 303 cc. 10r-15r (Manus 691092): the heading says the letter 'fu acchiarita dal Mastro della Cifra di S. M.ta Christ.ma'; incipit 'N.ro Sig.re ha inteso quello che v. Emi.za scrive li 10, e 17 Maggio'. (2) Florence, ASF, Carte Strozziane, serie I, cc. 233-238, from the printed inventory of 1891: 'cifra di Mons.r N. Secretario di Stato di Sua S.ta mandata al Sig.re Card.le Bichi Nunzio in Francia, che fu intercetta dal Gover.re di Lione, e presentata nel suo Consiglio. Comincia: Nostro Signore ha inteso quello che V. Em.za scrive in lettere de x et 17 maggio'. (3) Naples, Biblioteca Oratoriana (Girolamini), in a political miscellany with Pasquinades and the 1630 Milan plague relations (Mandarini, I codici manoscritti della Biblioteca oratoriana di Napoli, 1897): '... di Mons. Segretario di Stato di S.a S.a mandata al Card. Bichi Nontio in Francia. Da Roma'. (4) A further copy listed in Gli archivi della storia d'Italia (1907), next to a 'Discorso intorno alla comprotezione di Francia' dated 10 May 1634. The text is therefore the plain Italian letter, deciphered by the French king's cipher master (Rossignol's office) and spread from the royal council. Bichi is styled cardinal (created 28 Nov 1633) and still nuncio, and the letter answers his letters of 10 and 17 May, which dates it to late May or June 1634, not 'c. 1630-1634'. The Ambrosiana leaves themselves were not seen (OPAC behind a JS bot check, no folios, no images, no browser used), so whether X 279 inf. holds the clear copy, like every other known copy, is unproven. Either way the letter's decipherment is on record, which is what the vetting bar's 'read' means. Besancon Chiflet f. 254 ('interceptee et dechiffree', dated 1641 by CCFr) may be yet another copy.
